newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan real estate good investment, say U.S. firms.
newsitem.headline: Japan real estate good investment, say U.S. firms.

text.p: The Japanese real estate market is currently a good investment, although regulatory changes are needed before this can have much impact on the nation's economic recovery, representatives of major U.S. investment firms said.

"Japanese stock and real estate markets are on the verge of becoming the buys of the rest of the century," Richard Medley, president of Medley Investment Group, told a Japanese parliamentary study group at the headquarters of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party on Wednesday.
He said Japanese commercial land prices are down more than 80 percent from their peak in 1991, making them potentially good buys.
He also cited foreign interest in recent auctions of land belonging to the former Japanese National Railways.

In one, a Japanese unit of Pacific Century Group bought land near Tokyo Station for a far higher price than analysts had forecast. Pacific Century Group is headed by Hong Kong-born businessman Richard Li.

Medley's comments were echoed by Robert Dugger, director of Tudor Investment Corp. "We believe that the real estate market in Japan has bottomed out and if the government can successfully get land into the market, the stock market also will have bottomed out," he said.
But he warned that deregulation is needed for a true land price recovery that will boost the economy overall as well.

Key changes would include the elimination of all tax obstacles to real estate sales as well as allowing the securitisation of real estate assets, he said. "The success of the banking recovery in the U.S. was the direct result of American businesses being able to securitise real estate assets," Dugger said.
Both Medley and Dugger acknowledged that there is overseas cynicism about Japan's proposed "Big Bang" financial market deregulation but said Japan must pursue such changes actively.
"The (role of the) financial centre of Asia is up for grabs and if Japan moves swiftly to seize this opportunity it can and will become the financial centre of Asia," Dugger said.
